saints.name: St. Paulinus of Nola
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman senator and poet who gave away his wealth to serve Christ and the tomb of St. Felix…
biography: Born about 354 at Bordeaux into a senatorial family with estates across Gaul, Spain, and Italy, Pontius Meropius Paulinus was schooled by the poet Ausonius and rose to be suffect consul about 377 and governor of Campania, where he first honored the martyr Felix of Nola, building a road and a hospice for pilgrims to his tomb.

After the Emperor Gratian's murder in 383 he withdrew from public life, married Therasia of Barcelona, and was baptized by Delphinus of Bordeaux. When their only child died eight days after birth, the pair renounced their fortune. Ordained priest at Barcelona about 394, he settled the next year at Nola beside Felix's tomb, restoring its basilicas and honoring the saint's feast each year with a new poem.

After Therasia's death he was chosen bishop of Nola about 409 and governed some twenty years, corresponding with Augustine, Jerome, and Sulpicius Severus; Augustine sent him his works to be copied in Italy. He died on 22 June 431. Later ages credited him with the first church bells, whence the old bell-names nola and campana.
saints.knownFor: His poetry and his renunciation of wealth for Christ.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 22 June
